title: Inside the Computer
subject: Computer Science
description: In this activity, you will open a computer's system unit and explore the parts inside it. Tip: Move the device around to see the parts from different angles.

observe.description: Observe the parts inside a computer's system unit and what each one does.

captions.text: A computer is made of parts that work together. They take in data, process it, store it, and give out information.
Most of these parts live inside the system unit. Let's take off the side panel and look inside.
The large circuit board at the back is the motherboard. Every other part connects to it, so they can share power and data.
In the middle is the central processing unit, or CPU. It carries out instructions and does calculations. It is the brain of the computer.
The CPU gets hot as it works, so a heat sink and fan sit on top of it to carry the heat away.
Beside the CPU are the memory modules, called RAM. RAM holds the programs and data the computer is using right now.
RAM is volatile. When the power goes off, everything in it is lost.
Programs and files are kept for a long time on drives, like this solid-state drive and this hard disk drive. They keep their data even without power.
The graphics card turns data into the pictures you see on the monitor.
The power supply unit changes electricity from the wall socket into the steady, low voltages the parts need.
Fans keep the air moving through the case, so all the parts stay cool.
Together, these parts let the computer do its work. Now it is your turn to take them out.

explore.description: Take the system unit apart. Drag each part to its tray to learn what it does.

parts.name: CPU cooler
parts.text: a heat sink and fan that carry heat away from the processor, so it does not overheat.

parts.name: CPU
parts.text: the central processing unit. It carries out instructions and does calculations: the brain of the computer.

parts.name: RAM
parts.text: main memory. It holds the programs and data in use right now, and is cleared when the power goes off.

parts.name: Graphics card
parts.text: turns data into the images and video shown on the monitor.

parts.name: Power supply unit
parts.text: changes mains electricity from the wall into the low, steady voltages the parts need.

parts.name: Solid-state drive
parts.text: stores programs and files permanently in flash memory, with no moving parts.

parts.name: Hard disk drive
parts.text: stores programs and files permanently on spinning magnetic disks.

parts.name: Case fan
parts.text: pulls cool air into the case and pushes hot air out.

items.q: Which part carries out instructions and does calculations?
What happens to the data in RAM when the computer is switched off?
answers: It stays until it is deleted

items.q: Which part keeps your files when the computer is turned off?
What is the main job of the power supply unit?
answers: To change mains electricity into low voltages for the parts
To show pictures on the monitor

items.q: Which board connects all the parts so they can share power and data?
Why does the CPU have a heat sink and fan on top of it?
answers: To carry heat away so it does not overheat

items.q: Which part turns data into the images shown on the monitor?
RAM is called volatile memory because...
answers: it needs power to keep its data

items.q: How is a solid-state drive different from a hard disk drive?
answers: It loses its data without power
It is a kind of RAM

items.q: Which part is called the brain of the computer?
